name: Jean Charles Samuelian
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Alan (French digital health insurer)
profile: Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve co-founded Paris-based health insurer Alan in 2016 and has led it since. Alan sells digital-first health insurance and prevention services in France, Belgium, Spain and Canada; a €480M Series G valued it at about €5.5B. He is also an early backer and board member of Mistral AI.
interesting_fact: Alan's 2026 Series G raised €480M (~$550M) at a ~€5.5B valuation to expand into Canada's group-benefits market; the company reported >€800M ARR and >1.1M members.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alan he co-founded Expliseat, maker of the 'Titanium Seat' economy airline seat that cut seat weight by about two-thirds; it earned him the French Industry Medal and two Montgolfier prizes. He is also a Founders Pledge member.
notes: Also appears as Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve. Alan press room is the best formal route; he speaks often at French tech events (VivaTech, Paris Fintech Forum).

name: Adrien Nussenbaum
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Mirakl (stepped back from co-CEO role in 2026)
profile: HEC Paris graduate and serial founder who co-founded Mirakl with Philippe Corrot in 2012; Mirakl's marketplace and dropship SaaS is used by retailers such as Best Buy, Carrefour and Galeries Lafayette and was valued around $3.5-4B. After leaving executive duties in 2026 he became Mirakl's chairman (announced 10 Nov 2026), focusing more on philanthropy and film production.
interesting_fact: Mirakl's Nov 2026 governance change named him Chairman and said he will devote more time to philanthropy and film production, while ex-Sitecore CEO Steve Tzikakis took over his co-CEO remit.
deep_cut_fact: Before Mirakl he founded All Instant, a New York instant-messaging platform sold in 2003, then with Corrot built SplitGames, a video-game marketplace sold to Fnac in 2008, after which the pair designed Fnac.com's marketplace - the blueprint for Mirakl.
notes: Now non-executive; film production and philanthropy are new interests - a possible angle. No published press email found on Mirakl newsroom; approach via Mirakl comms/newsroom or LinkedIn.

name: Zhang Shijie
current_role: Chief Scientist, GalaxySpace (银河航天), per Chinese press; not the company's founder/CEO
profile: Hurun lists Zhang Shijie (张世杰) as a GalaxySpace founder, but public reporting names Xu Ming (ex-Cheetah Mobile CTO/president) as GalaxySpace's founder, chairman and CEO (22% stake, ~73% voting control). Zhang is quoted as GalaxySpace's chief scientist, describing its stackable flat-panel satellites and ~1mm-thick flexible solar wings. GalaxySpace began A-share IPO tutoring in March 2026.
interesting_fact: Zhang has explained that GalaxySpace builds stackable flat-panel satellites with foldable solar wings over 2.5m wide but only ~1mm thick, so dozens of satellites can be stacked and launched at once to cut per-satellite launch cost.
notes: Hurun attribution looks off: GalaxySpace's founder is Xu Ming (徐鸣). A Harbin Institute of Technology satellite professor named Zhang Shijie (b.1979) exists, but no source links him to GalaxySpace - same-name risk, so not used. Company IPO prep reported by cls.cn (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2330307).

name: Waseem Daher
current_role: Co-founder, Pilot.com (CEO per most bios; some 2026 directories list him as Executive Chair)
profile: MIT computer-science graduate and three-time founder. He co-founded Ksplice (rebootless Linux updates, sold to Oracle in 2011) and Zulip (team chat, sold to Dropbox in 2014), then in 2017 co-founded Pilot with fellow MIT alumni. Pilot provides bookkeeping, tax and CFO services for startups and was valued at about $1.2B.
interesting_fact: He and his MIT co-founders Jessica McKellar and Jeff Arnold have now started three companies together: Ksplice, Zulip and Pilot.
deep_cut_fact: Ksplice, which grew out of Jeff Arnold's MIT master's thesis, won the top prize in the 20th annual MIT $100K Entrepreneurship Competition in May 2009; Daher (MIT '07, MEng '08) was one of its four co-founders.
notes: Talks openly about frameworks for validating startup ideas (First Round Review podcast ep. 27). Current title unclear (CEO vs Executive Chair) - check before outreach.

name: Olivier Pailhès
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Aircall (returned as CEO on 29 Oct 2026, succeeding Scott Chancellor)
profile: HEC Paris MBA and ex-BCG/ArcelorMittal staffer who co-founded Paris-based cloud phone company Aircall in 2014 with three partners and ran it until 2023, then stayed on the board. He returned as CEO in October 2026 to push Aircall, now at $250M ARR and 24,000+ customers, into AI voice agents.
interesting_fact: On returning as CEO he framed the bet as: 'AI has handed us a rare opportunity; to bring voice back to the center of customer conversations.' Aircall was valued at about $1B+ in its 2021 round.
deep_cut_fact: He is an accomplished pianist - Aircall's own announcement says the Paris team knows that an unscheduled jazz performance usually means the founder is in the building.
notes: Very timely: just returned as CEO (Oct 2026) with an AI-voice-agent agenda. Press contact is Aircall's published media contact on that release.

name: Levi Cooperman
current_role: Co-founder of FreshBooks (later Government Relations); Crunchbase lists him as a partner at RevvWorks (not confirmed on RevvWorks' own site)
profile: Levi Cooperman co-founded Toronto cloud-accounting company FreshBooks in 2003-04 with Mike McDerment and Joe Sawada, early on quitting his job to work on it full time and later serving as VP Operations and in government relations. FreshBooks, used by millions of small businesses, reached a ~$1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: FreshBooks was founded in Toronto by McDerment, Cooperman and Sawada and grew from a small-business invoicing tool into a unicorn cloud accounting platform.
deep_cut_fact: Before FreshBooks he was a professional engineer (BEng, University of Victoria) who managed systems-integration projects at Apex Systems Integrators for clients including Canadian Tire, Nestle and Parmalat.
notes: Low public profile. The FreshBooks author bio used for the deep-cut fact now returns 404 (archived Nov 2024 on web.archive.org). No published personal/office contact found; RevvWorks lists only a generic info@revv.works and does not name him.

name: Sergey Barysiuk
profile: Belarusian-born engineer (also spelled Siarhei Barysiuk / Sergey Borisyuk) who, with Mikita Mikado, turned their Minsk software-outsourcing shop's sales-quote tool Quote Roller (c.2011) into PandaDoc, a document automation and e-signature platform. PandaDoc reached a $1B valuation in 2021 and is now headquartered in San Francisco with large teams in Europe.
interesting_fact: PandaDoc began life as Quote Roller, a set of proposal templates sent as a link, before broadening into all business documents and e-signatures and becoming one of the first Belarus-founded unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: He says the idea came on 'a warm June evening' at their outsourcing firm, when he was about to go home and got buried in contracts and proposals to write - as 'a true developer' who disliked paperwork, he decided the process had to be automated.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; Mikado is the public face. Company relocated staff out of Belarus after 2020 (sensitive political context - avoid in outreach). PandaDoc site blocked automated fetch; no press email confirmed.

name: Hesham El Nahhas
current_role: Co-founder, Wrapbook (listed as Co-Founder & Chief People Officer as of the 2021 Series B; current title unconfirmed)
profile: Hesham El-Nahhas is one of four co-founders (with Ali Javid, Cameron Woodward and Naysawn Naji) of Wrapbook, founded in 2018 to digitise payroll, onboarding and insurance for film, TV and commercial productions. Wrapbook raised a $27M Series A led by a16z and a $100M Series B led by Tiger Global in Nov 2021 at a $1B valuation.
interesting_fact: Wrapbook's backers include Hollywood figures Jeffrey Katzenberg (WndrCo) and CAA co-founder Michael Ovitz; a16z said at its Series A the company was growing revenue about 7x year-over-year.
notes: Spelled El-Nahhas in company materials. Very low individual public profile; CEO Ali Javid is the company's public face. Wrapbook press center (https://www.wrapbook.com/press) lists no press email.

name: Luke Li
current_role: Co-founder of Amber Group (in charge of trading); Director of Nasdaq-listed Amber International Holding (AMBR) since Aug 2025
profile: Tsinghua economics/applied-maths grad with a Columbia master's in financial engineering, Luke Li was a credit strategist on Morgan Stanley's Hong Kong fixed-income desk (2015-18) before co-founding crypto trading and liquidity firm Amber Group, which hit unicorn status in 2021. He runs Amber's trading business and joined the board of its listed arm Amber International in 2025.
interesting_fact: Five of Amber's six founders, including Li, worked together on Morgan Stanley's Hong Kong fixed-income floor; in 2015, all in their 20s, they started a side project running algorithmic trading on Chinese stocks and index futures before going full-time into crypto arbitrage.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a bachelor's in economics, finance and applied mathematics from Tsinghua (2013) and a master's in financial engineering from Columbia (2014), and is described as a trusted advisor to multiple leading crypto projects.

public_contacts.value: Paradigm Consulting (Asia): ambr@paradigmconsulting.com.hk; International Elite Capital (US): amber@iecapitalusa.com

notes: Common name - identity anchored by Amber International's Aug 2025 PR Newswire release. Low public profile; route via Amber International PR/IR.

name: Thomas Vaughan
current_role: Co-founder, Upside (formerly GetUpside), Washington DC; current title not publicly confirmed
profile: Thomas Vaughan is one of six co-founders of Upside, the Washington DC cash-back app (gas, groceries, restaurants) launched in 2016 that pays consumers from retailers' incremental margin; it was valued around $1.9B in 2021. The founding team came together at Opower, the utility customer-engagement software company Oracle bought for $532M in 2016.
interesting_fact: Upside's model gets fuel stations, grocers and restaurants to fund personalised cash-back offers only on incremental profit, and users have earned hundreds of millions of dollars in cash back.
deep_cut_fact: Before Upside he worked at Opower, the energy-efficiency/utility engagement software firm, where he met CEO Alex Kinnier and the other co-founders; they left together after Oracle acquired Opower in 2016 - a natural energy-industry angle.
notes: Very low individual profile; common name - identity anchored only via company co-founder lists. No published press email found on Upside newsroom; CEO Alex Kinnier is the company's public face.

name: Dan Amiga
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Island (enterprise browser), Dallas/Tel Aviv
profile: Israeli Unit 8200 veteran who co-founded Fireglass (remote browser isolation), sold to Symantec in 2017, then co-founded Island with CEO Mike Fey in 2020. Island built the first enterprise browser - Chromium-based with built-in security and IT controls - and was valued at about $5B in 2025; Amiga now pushes its AI-governance products.
interesting_fact: He is credited with inventing two security categories: remote browser isolation at Fireglass and the 'enterprise browser' at Island, backed by Sequoia, Insight, Coatue and Cyberstarts.
deep_cut_fact: At Black Hat USA 2016 (Aug 3, Mandalay Bay) he and Dor Knafo presented 'Account Jumping: Post Infection Persistency & Lateral Movement in AWS', showing how attackers could evade CloudTrail auditing and persist in AWS accounts.

public_contacts.value: Andy Shane, Big Valley Marketing for Island: ashane@bigvalley.co

notes: Frequent conference speaker (RSA, Web Summit, Cybertech). Best route is Island's PR agency Big Valley Marketing.

name: Varun Alagh
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Honasa Consumer Ltd (Mamaearth parent; NSE/BSE listed)
profile: Delhi College of Engineering electrical engineer and XLRI MBA who spent years in FMCG at Hindustan Unilever, Diageo and Coca-Cola before co-founding Honasa Consumer with Ghazal Alagh in 2016. Honasa grew Mamaearth into a house of brands (The Derma Co, Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's, BBlunt) and listed in India in Nov 2023. In Jan 2026 he joined Shark Tank India Season 5 as a Shark.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he joined Shark Tank India (Season 5, Sony TV) as one of the Sharks, alongside Ghazal Alagh who was a Shark in earlier seasons.
deep_cut_fact: During his corporate career he was instrumental in launching Coke Zero in India, and won Diageo's 'I am Diageo' and 'Above and Beyond' awards.
notes: High public profile in India (TV, LinkedIn). Honasa is a listed company, so IR/stock-exchange filings also available. Avoid child-related origin story in outreach.
